title: Inside an Autumn Pumpkin
description: Look inside a pumpkin through familiar words for its parts and the objects used around a seasonal display.
cardDescription: Look inside a pumpkin through familiar words for its parts and the objects used around a seasonal display.
focus: The clues describe plant structures and household objects. Their location or purpose identifies the answer.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names an outer covering, an inner part, or a utensil.
words: Large squash commonly associated with Halloween displays
One small plant structure found inside a pumpkin
Soft moist flesh within a fruit
Firm outer covering of a pumpkin
One threadlike strand within a pumpkin’s interior
Short plant support attached at the top of a pumpkin
Rounded tool used to lift soft material
Bowl-ended utensil that can lift pumpkin seeds
Absorbent cloth laid beside a kitchen project
Utensil that separates small solids from liquid
Color commonly associated with a ripe display pumpkin
Curved all around, as the shape of many pumpkins

answerNotes.PULP: Pulp names soft fruit material. It differs from the firm outer rind.
answerNotes.RIND: The rind is the outside covering. The clue contrasts that location with the inner cavity.
answerNotes.CAVITY: A cavity is a hollow space. The word is used for an object’s interior rather than a dental condition here.
answerNotes.FIBER: Fiber is one threadlike strand in this clue. The singular form names a small part of the interior.

title: The Costume Closet
description: Open a costume closet through familiar garments, accessories, and the details that fasten them.
cardDescription: Open a costume closet through familiar garments, accessories, and the details that fasten them.
focus: The clues describe clothing and simple theatrical objects. Ordinary shapes and body locations provide the meaning.
solvingTip: Look for a whole garment, an accessory, or a clothing part.
words: Outfit worn to represent a character at a seasonal party
Covering that changes or conceals the face
Sleeveless outer garment hanging from the shoulders
Head covering used as part of an outfit
Hand covering with individual finger sections
Head decoration suggesting a royal character
Broad decorative band worn around the body
Fastener passed through a garment’s small opening
Clothing closure operated by a sliding pull
Sewn compartment used to carry a small object

answerNotes.CAPE: A cape hangs from the shoulders without sleeves. Its shape distinguishes it from a fitted coat.
answerNotes.SASH: A sash is a broad band. It may cross the body or encircle the waist depending on the outfit.
answerNotes.WIG: A wig is a separate hairlike covering. It names an accessory rather than the wearer’s own hair.
answerNotes.CROWN: Crown is a costume object here. It does not mean the top of a tooth or the upper part of a hat.

description: Set out a seasonal snack table with familiar sweets, serving objects, and wrapping words.
cardDescription: Set out a seasonal snack table with familiar sweets, serving objects, and wrapping words.
focus: The clues identify food forms and the objects holding them. Some ordinary words can name either a texture or a whole item.

Sweet made by heating sugar, often combined with dairy ingredients

answerNotes.CARAMEL: Caramel involves heated sugar. It names the sweet material rather than the apple it may cover.
answerNotes.PRETZEL: A pretzel is recognizable by its twisted form. The clue uses shape rather than a particular brand.
answerNotes.WRAP: Wrap is an outer covering in this clue. It is a noun rather than an instruction to cover something.
answerNotes.TREAT: A treat is something enjoyed or given as a small pleasure. The party setting narrows its meaning to food offered to a guest.

title: A Walk at Twilight
description: Follow a seasonal evening walk through familiar light, weather, and entrance words.
cardDescription: Follow a seasonal evening walk through familiar light, weather, and entrance words.
focus: The clues describe what a person might notice around a neighborhood at dusk. Positions and changes in light distinguish the terms.
solvingTip: Look for a time of day, a light effect, a place, or a movement.
words: Time when daylight is fading toward night
Earth’s natural satellite visible in many evening skies
Dark shape made when an object blocks light
Portable light enclosed in a protective housing
One raised level leading to a doorway
Flat plant part sometimes found underfoot in autumn
Light wind felt during an evening walk
Period of partial light before night or after dawn
Dark portion of the daily cycle
Soft steady light from a lamp or decoration
To move along a neighborhood route on foot

answerNotes.TWILIGHT: Twilight is partial daylight near sunrise or sunset. The evening setting here points toward the start of night.
answerNotes.SHADOW: A shadow results from blocked light. It differs from the light source making it visible.
answerNotes.GLOW: Glow is a soft steady light in this clue. It does not require a sharp flashing pattern.
answerNotes.LANTERN: A lantern encloses a light source. The clue names the whole portable object rather than its flame or bulb.

description: Explore familiar seasonal images through animals, story figures, and traditional decorative objects.
cardDescription: Explore familiar seasonal images through animals, story figures, and traditional decorative objects.
focus: The clues describe symbols used in displays and stories. Fictional figures are identified as story characters rather than real beings.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names an animal, an object, or a traditional imaginary figure.
words: Flying mammal often represented in Halloween decorations
Bird commonly pictured with large forward-facing eyes
Domestic feline often shown in seasonal silhouettes
Eight-legged animal associated with a silken web
Silken structure made by many spiders
Sweeping tool associated with a witch in traditional stories
Magic-using figure in folklore and Halloween stories
Spirit figure represented in traditional spooky stories

Round or crescent sky symbol used in evening decorations

Harvest crop whose dried stalks may decorate a doorway
Dried forage arranged in bales for some fall displays

answerNotes.BAT: Bats are mammals, although they fly. Their animal group distinguishes them from birds such as owls.
answerNotes.SPIDER: Spiders have eight legs. They are arachnids rather than six-legged insects.
answerNotes.WEB: Web names a silken animal structure here. It does not refer to the internet.
answerNotes.GHOST: Ghost names a figure in traditional stories and decorations. The clue concerns the fictional or folkloric image.
